subject: Marlin model: elevated 502/504 cascade — incident updates and closure
messages:

Subject: Marlin model: elevated 502/504 cascade — initial alert

Hi Sam —

Thanks for flagging the spike this morning. Our SREs have confirmed an elevated rate of 502/504s originating from the Marlin (rw-marlin-13b) routing pool beginning at ~08:50 PT. We believe this is a cascade triggered by slow KV cache thrashing under a sudden throughput burst for requests with long context windows.

Immediate steps we are taking (already in motion):
- Redirecting a portion of OptiCore traffic to Marlin-quant-2 (a compatible, lower-memory variant) to reduce backpressure.
- Throttling large-batch pipelines that hit long-context endpoints (temporary limit enforced).
- Engaging runtime engineers to capture full trace samples and the affected kernel logs.

Irene is on the kernel sampling now and Ben is coordinating the customer-facing reroute. We’ll send an update within the hour. Apologies for the disruption — we know you rely on these endpoints for live scoring.

Avery Johnson

Quick internal note —

Observed details:
- Spike window: 08:50–09:30 PT (peak at 09:03)
- Error mix: 62% 502 gateway, 28% 504 upstream timeout, 10% 5xx other
- Correlation: 83% of affected requests include long-context (≥12k tokens) and heavy KV cache churn tags

Actions taken:
- Traffic split: 65% -> marlin-quant-2, 35% -> rw-marlin-13b (reduced max concurrent requests)
- Autoscaler adjusted to avoid aggressive bin-packing; ramped another 10 nodes in the pool
- Collected traces and KV cache hit/miss series (linked to INF-3912)

Next: kernel team to validate hot-loop in attention transpose path (Irene). If we can confirm a cache eviction storm, we’ll ship a fast mitigation gate to prefer smaller batch sizes for long-context requests.

Ben
Sr. SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-12T10:10:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Marlin model: elevated 502/504 cascade — initial alert

Folks —

Kernel sampling shows repeated stall events inside the KV cache write path when per-request KV allocations spike. The pattern fits a cascading eviction where new contexts displace cached prefixes frequently, causing synchronous IO backpressure on the worker. Patch plan:
- Short term (hours): enforce per-request KV ceiling for rw-marlin-13b (temporary config flip) and prefer marlin-quant-2 for heavy-context calls.
- Mid term (days): adjust allocator heuristics to reduce eviction churn; add async eviction path to relieve synchronous stalls.

I’ll attach diagnostic snippets to INF-3912; capturing full repro traces for the team to validate.

Irene
Kernel Engineer, Serving Runtime

Subject: Marlin model: incident closure and postmortem next steps

Sam —

Quick closure note and next steps:

What happened (brief):
- A sudden throughput burst hitting long-context requests caused repeated KV cache evictions on rw-marlin-13b workers. Eviction churn led to synchronous stalls and upstream timeouts (502/504 mix).

Immediate mitigations applied:
- Traffic split to marlin-quant-2 and temporary KV ceiling on rw-marlin-13b (08/12 09:00 PT) — reduced error rate from 7.3% to 0.7% within 18 minutes.
- Autoscaler adjustments and additional worker nodes to reduce bin-packing pressure.

Root cause (summary):
- Runtime allocation heuristic allowed high per-request KV residency under rare burst patterns; eviction behavior introduced synchronous IO backpressure in the attention path.

Remediations and timelines:
- Short term (today–48h): keep KV ceiling in place; maintain redirected traffic for high-context routes. We will coordinate a maintenance window if you want the ceiling toggled.
- Medium term (7–14 days): kernel patch to change eviction from synchronous to async for large KV churn plus allocator heuristic tweak (Irene & kernel team).
- Long term (4–8 weeks): improved load-profiling to automatically route heavy long-context workloads to quant variants and expanded monitoring (alerts on KV miss churn).

Attachments: marlin_error_rates_20260812-14.png; draft postmortem at https://drive.redwood.com/drive/u/0/folders/1MarlinIncidentDocs (marlin_postmortem_draft_v1.docx attached).

We’ll circulate the completed postmortem (final version) once kernel validations are done; target for publication: 2026-08-20. Please let us know if you’d like a call to walk through the RCA and planned mitigations — we can schedule one tomorrow morning PT.

Thanks again for your patience and for immediately flagging the issue.
